question.problem:
Consider the functions $y(x)=Ax$ and $f(y)=By,$ where $x\in {R}^{3},y\in {R}^{2},$ and the matrices $A$ and $B$ are given by $$ A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]. $$ What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[0,\,-1,\,1]^{T}?$
${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))|}_{{x}_{0}}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
$6$ {{field-4}} $3$

current_example.problem:
Consider the functions $\mathbf{y}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{B}\mathbf{y},$ where $\mathbf x\in \mathbb R^3, \mathbf y\in\mathbb R^2,$ and the matrices $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/8d2943532f2ab5d5f153bd6f27ad285a25fc9d7ddf6727ccbc2af74bea4fdeda.svg)
What is $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \mathbf x} \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}(\mathbf x))$ evaluated at $\mathbf{x}_0 = [1, \, 0, \, -2]^T?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \mathbf x} \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}(\mathbf x)) = \dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf f}{\textrm d \mathbf y} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf y}{\textrm d \mathbf x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $\mathbf{f}$ acts on a vector $\mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ by multiplying it by $\mathbf{B}$ and outputs a vector $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}) \in \mathbb{R}^3.$ Thus,

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf f}{\textrm d \mathbf y} = \mathbf{B}.
$$

- The function $\mathbf{y}$ acts on a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ by multiplying it by $\mathbf{A}$ and outputs a vector $\mathbf{y}(\mathbf{x}) \in \mathbb{R}^2.$ Thus,

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf y}{\textrm d \mathbf x} = \mathbf{A}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x)) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \\  & =BA \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & -6 & 1 \\ 20 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
